Conductor

The Conductor is the control boundary between a and the Pipeline. It receives state resolution requests, serializes them through a FIFO queue, delegates controller arbitration to the Decision Engine, and routes approved attempts into the Orchestrator for Pipeline execution.

The Conductor guarantees that every state transition for a is processed one at a time, in order, with full controller evaluation before any Pipeline stage executes.

Conductor Responsibility

The Conductor serves as the single entry point for all state resolution requests targeting a . Its responsibilities are narrowly scoped:

  • Serialization — All incoming attempts are enqueued in strict FIFO order. Only one attempt may be active at any time.
  • Controller delegation — Each attempt is evaluated by the Decision Engine and its registered Controllers before Pipeline execution begins.
  • Routing — Approved attempts are forwarded to the Orchestrator for deterministic Pipeline execution.
  • Lifecycle management — The Conductor coordinates initialization, reset, and destruction of both Behaviors and Controllers.

The Conductor does not perform state derivation, does not participate in Pipeline stage execution, and does not modify candidate values. It operates exclusively as a coordination and control boundary.

Lifecycle Coordination

The Conductor manages the full lifecycle of a 's pipeline infrastructure:

Operation Behavior
Initialize Enqueues the initial state load as the first pipeline attempt. Controllers and Behaviors are constructed and registered before the first attempt is processed.
Reset Clears the attempt queue, resets all registered Behaviors, and resets all registered Controllers. The returns to its pre-initialization state without destruction.
Destroy Clears the attempt queue, invokes destroy on all Behaviors and Controllers, and completes all internal event streams. The Conductor is terminal after destruction.
Calling methods on a destroyed Conductor is invalid. Once destroyed, the cannot be reactivated. Register a new if the feature remounts.
Controller Arbitration

Before any Pipeline stage executes, the Conductor submits the active attempt to the Decision Engine for controller evaluation. Controllers vote on whether the attempt should proceed, be denied, or be aborted.

The Decision Engine aggregates controller votes and produces a single normalized outcome that determines the Conductor's next action. Controller evaluation is deterministic — given identical state and configuration, the same outcome is always produced.

Controllers registered with a participate in every attempt evaluation. They may implement policies such as rate limiting, circuit breakers, concurrency gates, or approval workflows.

Key point: Controllers evaluate policy before Pipeline execution. They do not participate in state derivation, filtering, reduction, or persistence. Their sole authority is over whether an attempt proceeds.
Execution Guarantees

The Conductor provides the following guarantees to all downstream Pipeline stages:

  • Strict serialization — Only one attempt is active at any time. No interleaving, no reentrancy, no race conditions.
  • FIFO ordering — Attempts are processed in the exact order they were received.
  • Controller-first evaluation — Every attempt passes through controller arbitration before any Pipeline Behavior executes.
  • Microtask finalization — Attempt completion occurs in a microtask boundary, ensuring clean turn isolation and preventing synchronous re-entry.
  • Deterministic settlement — In DevMode, the Conductor exposes a settlement signal that resolves when the queue has fully drained. This enables deterministic testing without timing hacks.
Testing implication: The settlement guarantee is what makes the three-step test pattern (mutate → await → assert) work. vaultSettled(key) resolves when the Conductor's queue has fully drained and the final state snapshot is stable.
